chunks: Ja'far b. 'Ali b. al-Hasan b. 'Ali b. 'Abdullah b. al-Mughira al-Kufi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan b. 'Ali narrated to me from his grandfather 'Abdullah b. al-Mughira from Isma'il b. Muslim from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them).

He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: There are four things that will not enter a household — even one of them — except that it will be ruined and will not flourish with blessing: betrayal, theft, drinking wine, and adultery.

key_terms.الزِّنَا: adultery/fornication — unlawful sexual relations, considered among the gravest sins
key_terms.الْبَرَكَةُ: divine blessing/baraka — the spiritual abundance and prosperity that flows from God's favor
key_terms.الْخِيَانَةُ: betrayal/treachery — breach of trust in any relationship or responsibility

ai.seo_question: What four things does the Prophet say will ruin a household and remove blessing from it?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWA) identifies four destructive vices — betrayal, theft, drinking wine, and adultery — that, if any one of them enters a household, will cause it to fall into ruin and deprive it of divine blessing (baraka). This tradition was transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and his forefathers, emphasizing the Imams' role in preserving prophetic teachings. In the context of early Islamic society, these four vices were understood not merely as individual moral failures but as social diseases that corrupted the foundational unit of civilization — the family home.
